messages.subject: [statnet_help] visualizing networks?
messages.body_plain:
Hi statnet enthusiasts,

I wanted to create several visualizations of example networks that I am
creating with the statnet (plus igraph/intergraph). The network package has
a nice interface to the plot command to visualize a force-directed layout.
However I was wondering if there were R visualization packages that offer
more flexible visualization capabilities such as arc diagrams or matrix
diagrams. Any suggestions welcome!

Thanks,
Adrian

--

messages.subject: [statnet_help] visualizing networks?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Adrian,

I'm not sure what a matrix diagram is, but if I understand you then  
it's relatively easy to write R code from scratch to do something like  
that.  Here's a little snippet I wrote for a talk that plots an  
adjacency matrix as a white square with black entries where the arcs  
lie:

matplotter <- function(x) {
   if (is.network(x)) x <- x[,]
   n <- dim(x)[1]
   plot(0:n, n:0, type="n", xaxt="n", yaxt="n", xlab="",
        ylab="", bty="n", ylim=c(n,0))
   therows <- row(x)[x>0]
   thecols <- col(x)[x>0]
   rect(thecols-1, therows-1, thecols, therows, col=1)
   rect(0,0,n,n)
}

It should be easy to customize this in many ways (adding color,  
labels, etc.).  To see it used, try

library(ergm)
data(flo)
matplotter(flo)

Dave

Hi Adrian,

if this is what you want, you may also want to try the following commands:

image(flo)

#level plot:
library(lattice)
levelplot(flo)

#heat map:
heatmap(flo)

They can visualize valued networks as well.

Best,
Philip

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Problem specifying theta0 in simulate.ergm
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,
I am trying to simulate networks based on a ERG model with certain
coefficients fixed at null. In reading the simulate.ergm
documentation, this seems like it should be a fairly straightforward
matter using the theta0 arg. However, in working with the function I
can't quite get it to work. Here's a brief example to illustrate:


library(ergm)
library(network)
data(faux.magnolia.high)
ergm(faux.magnolia.high ~ edges + nodematch("Grade",diff=T) +
nodematch("Race",diff=T) + nodematch("Sex",diff=F) + absdiff("Grade")
+ gwesp(0.25,fixed=T))->mod
mod$coef->z
z[2:7]<- -50 #change all the nodematch grade coefs
simulate.ergm(mod,theta0=z)->new
ergm(new~edges + nodematch("Grade",diff=T) + nodematch("Race",diff=T)
+ nodematch("Sex",diff=F) + absdiff("Grade") +
gwesp(0.25,fixed=T))->mod.new
plot(mod$coef,mod.new$coef); abline(0,1)

Here's the start of the estimates from my machine:

> cbind(mod$coef,mod.new$coef)
                       [,1]   [,2]
edges                -8.275 -7.970
nodematch.Grade.7     1.579  0.836
nodematch.Grade.8     1.795  0.964

The two nodematch terms are certainly lower, but nowhere near where
they should be given the rather dramatic change I made to the vector
of coefficients. Any thoughts?

Thanks!
Ben Domingue
School of Education
CU Boulder
